Genealogies are relational graphs. Generation distance can be counted through parent links.

Maya is a parent of Noah. Noah is a parent of Lina. Maya is also a parent of Owen. Owen is a parent of Sara. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.

A parent is one generation above a child. A grandparent is two parent-links above. People who share a parent are siblings under this simplified model. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
What family relation between Maya and Lina follows from the stated links? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
1. Maya→Noah is one parent link. 2. Noah→Lina is a second parent link. 3. Two links give the grandparent relation. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00.
Maya is a grandparent of Lina. Cross-domain answer: 10:00.
Family relations can be derived step by step from a small set of explicit links.
Directed parent graph; kinship predicates derived from path length and shared ancestors.

Problem 686. Temporal compatibility in a story set in 1400
Anachronism can be tested as a compatibility problem when the relevant date ranges are supplied.

For this problem, availability intervals are: Technology A: 1200–1600; Institution B: 1500–1900; Tool C: 1700–2000; Practice D: 1300–1450. A story is set in 1400 and mentions Technology A and Tool C together. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 10 members, requires at least 6 present for quorum, and 8 are present.

An item is temporally compatible with a year only if the year lies inside its stated availability interval. An anachronism is an item placed outside its given interval. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Which mentioned item, if any, is anachronistic in the story? Cross-domain check: is quorum met?

1. Check 1400 against Technology A interval 1200–1600. 2. Check 1400 against Tool C interval 1700–2000. 3. Items outside their intervals: ['Tool C']. Cross-domain check: compare 8 with 6; 8≥6 is true.
Anachronistic: Tool C. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
The reasoning does not require memorizing invention dates if the intervals are part of the problem.
Interval membership test for each object-event pair.
